inputProvenance: Clean base before S1-07. The harness was tested with the uncommitted S1-07 change. These are hashes of actual file bytes; /proof hashes reported in the regression and both hybrid invocations matched the host files. The S1-06 evidence and certificate helper were not changed.
platform: linux/amd64 (x86_64) on Docker Desktop; existing image, no rebuild
commandPowerShell: docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --user 65534:65534 --tmpfs /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,nodev,size=1m,mode=0700,uid=65534,gid=65534 --mount "type=bind,source=$((Get-Location).Path)\spikes\tls,target=/proof,readonly" cafi-spikes:s1 python /proof/proof.py
commandNotes: Run from repository root with Docker Desktop's bin directory prepended to the process PATH. Append each run's arguments to the command. Each invocation creates a fresh container, Python process and ephemeral PKI. stdoutSHA256 below hashes captured UTF-8 stdout normalized to LF with a final LF.

runs.result: The updated harness returned the same policy and full seven case results as tls-x25519.json: two mTLS connections with ACK and x25519 observed at both ends, and five mTLS/SAN rejections without ACK.
Two mTLS connections with ACK and X25519MLKEM768 observed at both ends. Five mTLS/SAN rejections plus the group incompatibility rejection, all without ACK. See policy and cases below.
Independent repeat with fresh sockets and process. Both positive connections and all six rejections returned identical sanitized stdout to hybrid-1, including the policy and cases below.

The designated positive connection used the server CN instead of the SAN. SSL_connect failed (SSL_ERROR_SSL, certificate verify failed, X.509 code 62), the server received a fatal bad certificate alert, and the harness raised RuntimeError without success JSON or ACK.

supportMatrix.x25519mlkem768: Real TLS 1.3 mTLS and ACK; rejects X25519-only client

supportMatrix.x25519: Single group configured; x25519 observed on client and server
supportMatrix.x25519mlkem768: Single group configured; X25519MLKEM768 observed on client and server

supportMatrix.x25519: Certificate issuance only, no CLI handshake
supportMatrix.x25519mlkem768: Certificate issuance only, no CLI handshake

transport: Fresh TCP connections on 127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral listening port and fresh SSL objects per case. The two positive connections in each process reuse the same pair of SSL_CTX objects to check that resumption is disabled. The server writes an encrypted ACK only after both handshakes and identity checks succeed.
certificateFixtures: Two independent ephemeral laboratory CAs and role-specific P-256/SHA-256 leaves; both peers trust only lab-ca. Untrusted leaves keep the expected SAN. Wrong server identity tests CN instead of SAN; wrong client identity has a valid lab-ca chain and the expected CN but a different SAN. The group incompatibility case uses the same trusted client and the same hybrid server context as the positive cases.

observation.group: SSL_get0_group_name on both live, successfully handshaken SSL objects. The harness fails on a missing symbol, NULL, or an unexpected group; it does not substitute configured values.
observation.peerValidation: SSL_VERIFY_PEER in both roles, SSL_VERIFY_FAIL_IF_NO_PEER_CERT on the server. SSL_set1_host without wildcard or CN fallback; SSL_get0_peername, SSL_get_verify_result, SSL_get0_peer_certificate and SSL_get0_verified_chain confirm identity and trust.
observation.certificateAlgorithm: X509_get0_pubkey, EVP_PKEY_get0_type_name, EVP_PKEY_get_group_name and X509_get_signature_nid / OBJ_nid2sn. prime256v1 denotes P-256; ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256 is the only allowed handshake signature algorithm.
observation.session: SSL_session_reused, SSL_SESSION_has_ticket, SSL_SESSION_is_resumable and SSL_get_early_data_status are checked on both ends before and after the ACK.
observation.rejection: SSL_get_error and the OpenSSL error queue are sampled on the calling thread; SSL_get_verify_result is recorded. Where the client finishes locally before a client-certificate rejection, a subsequent read must receive a fatal TLS alert, not application data.
observation.incompatibility: The single-group context setup succeeds on both sides before a TCP connection is opened. SSL_accept fails with no suitable key share and SSL_connect receives the fatal handshake_failure alert. Neither succeeds; no application ACK is sent. X.509 code 0 here is not proof of certificate verification: group negotiation failed before peer authentication.

clientHandshake.verifyReason: unable to get local issuer certificate

serverHandshake.verifyReason: unable to get local issuer certificate

serverHandshake.reason: peer did not return a certificate

limitations: Only key establishment is hybrid; neither TLS certificates nor TLS authentication are post-quantum. The CLI only issues throwaway certificates in the restricted tmpfs. No private keys, certificates, TLS secrets or raw application payload bytes are retained in evidence; no message-signing key is used.
Both roles use the same OpenSSL build within each process, over real loopback TCP. No cross-implementation interoperability, external terminator, or separate-process endpoints were tested.

No active PSK/0-RTT injection, on-path manipulation, revocation, application authorization or identity-to-senderId binding, financial integration, or production stack decision. This is only the isolated TLS part of SPEC T08.
